newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA SHARES END LOWER ON FOREIGN SELLING.
newsitem.headline: MANILA SHARES END LOWER ON FOREIGN SELLING.

text.p: Manila stocks fell for the fourth straight day on Tuesday due to foreign selling of blue chips as the market continued to be hounded by high interest rates, brokers said.

"There's follow-through selling. We still have a high interest rate regime, weak corporate earnings. There's basically a lack of momentum to drive the shares upwards," said Corazon Guidote, UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd head of Philippine equities.
The main index closed lower by 37.03 points, or 1.44 percent, at 2,535.40 points.
The market index was at its lowest since July 10 before the peso had a de facto devaluation.

"The fundamental reason why the market is falling is that high interest rates will mean slower growth for the companies. If the central bank fails to find the right level, this will kill us brokers," said Jonathan Ravelas, head of sales at Asian Capital Equities.
Turnover was heavier at 2.2 billion pesos against 1.83 billion. All indices closed lower except for the oil shares sub-index which ended steady.
The market's barometer fell through its 2,550 support in mid-trade and was unable to recover in the remaining session.
In the broad market, losers outnumbered gainers 81 to 42 with 68 issues unchanged.
The blue chips that suffered from foreign selling were Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, San Miguel Corp B, Manila Electric Co B and Ayala Land Inc.

"The market will continue to be weak until it finds a more comfortable support where it should hold. The macroeconomic outlook on inflation and gross national product for the remaining half of the year give no reason for people to buy right now," said Henry Ong, trader at Sapphire Securities.
Traders expect the market to test support below 2,500 in the coming days.
